# Import pkgs 

```{r}
if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
  boot,          # For bootstrapping
  paralle,       # For parallel processing
  scales,        # For labels
  arrow,          # For reading the Parquet file
  broom,        # Convert model outputs to tidy tibbles
  tidyverse,      # Core data science tools: dplyr, ggplot2, etc. 
  glue,           # String interpolation 
  here,           # For reproducible file paths 
  purrr,          # Functional programming 
  estimatr,       # Robust regression 
  # effectsize,   # Effect size computation 
  sandwich,       # Robust standard errors 
  # ggrepel,      # Improved label placement in ggplot2 
  patchwork,      # Combine multiple ggplots 
  # ggpubr,       # Publication-ready plots 
  # corrplot,     # Correlation matrix plots
  # corrr,        # Tidy correlation workflows 
  correlation,  # Bayesian/frequentist correlation tests 
  modelsummary,   # Summarizing model outputs
  confintr,       # Confidence intervals 
  tinytable,     # Lightweight table formatting 
  binom          # For Wilson 95% CIs in get_predicted_percent_ci()
)

library("tidylog", warn.conflicts = FALSE)

devtools::install_github("graemeblair/stdidx")
library(stdidx)

options(es.use_symbols = TRUE) # get nice symbols

source(here("functions", "utils.r"))

ggplot2::theme_set(custom_theme())
```

# Import data 

```{r}
# Load individual organization-level data from Parquet file
org_df <- arrow::read_parquet(here("raw_data", "ind_org_df.parquet"))

# Load county-level aggregated datasets
cnts_counts_cov <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "cnty_counts_cov.csv"))          # Aggregated indicators and SDOH
cnts_civic_org_type <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "cnty_civic_org_type.csv"))  # Organizational type breakdown

# Load ZIP-level aggregated datasets
zcta_counts_cov <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "zcta_counts_cov.csv"))          # Aggregated indicators and SDOH
zcta_civic_org_type <- read_csv(here("data_outputs", "zcta_civic_org_type.csv"))  # Organizational type breakdown
```

```{r}
# Merge relevant SDOH variables into county-level organizational type data
cnts_civic_org_type <- cnts_civic_org_type %>%
  left_join(
    cnts_counts_cov %>%
      select(FIPS, POV150, SNGPNT, BROAD, NOHSDP, UNEMP, REMNRTY),
    by = c("FIPS" = "FIPS")
  )

# Merge relevant SDOH variables into ZIP-level organizational type data
zcta_civic_org_type <- zcta_civic_org_type %>%
  left_join(
    zcta_counts_cov %>%
      select(ZCTA, POV150, SNGPNT, BROAD, NOHSDP, UNEMP, REMNRTY),
    by = c("ZCTA")
  )
```

# Normalize SDOH variables (county and ZIP)

```{r}
# Normalize county-level SDOH indicators to range from 0 to 1
# This is min-max normalization: (x - min) / (max - min)
cnts_counts_cov <- cnts_counts_cov %>%
  mutate(
    POV150  = normalize(POV150),   # Poverty rate
    SNGPNT  = normalize(SNGPNT),   # Single-parent households
    BROAD   = normalize(BROAD),    # No broadband access
    NOHSDP  = normalize(NOHSDP),   # No high school diploma
    UNEMP   = normalize(UNEMP),    # Unemployment rate
    REMNRTY = normalize(REMNRTY)   # Racial/ethnic minority share
  )

# Apply the same min-max normalization to ZIP-level variables
zcta_counts_cov <- zcta_counts_cov %>%
  mutate(
    POV150  = normalize(POV150),
    SNGPNT  = normalize(SNGPNT),
    BROAD   = normalize(BROAD),
    NOHSDP  = normalize(NOHSDP),
    UNEMP   = normalize(UNEMP),
    REMNRTY = normalize(REMNRTY)
  )
```

# Validation

## The first dataset

```{r}
# This chunk evaluates whether "foundation" organizations are disproportionately likely to be classified as low or high civic opportunity types, based on their civic activity score.

org_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Compute civic_score: if all four civic indicators are missing or zero, set to NA
    civic_score = ifelse(
      (is.na(volunteer) & is.na(membership) & is.na(take_action) & is.na(events)) |
      (rowSums(across(c(volunteer, membership, take_action, events)), na.rm = TRUE) == 0),
      NA,
      idx_mean(volunteer, membership, take_action, events) # average across 4 binary indicators
    ),
    # Group civic_score into three categories
    civic_score_group = case_when(
      is.na(civic_score)        ~ "No Civic Score", 
      civic_score < 0.5         ~ "Low Civic Score",
      civic_score >= 0.5        ~ "Median or High Civic Score"
    ),
    # Set order for grouping factor
    civic_score_group = factor(civic_score_group, levels = c(
      "No Civic Score", "Low Civic Score", "Median or High Civic Score"
    ))
  ) %>%
  # Filter to organizations with a predicted class
  filter(!is.na(predicted)) %>%
  # Count rows by civic_score_group and predicted class
  group_by(civic_score_group, predicted) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Convert counts to proportions within each civic score group
  group_by(civic_score_group) %>%
  mutate(fraction = n / sum(n)) %>%
  # Filter to only show the "foundation" class
  filter(predicted == "foundation")
```

```{r}
# Generate bootstrapped financial summaries by civic score group
summary_df_long <- org_df %>%
  mutate(
    # Recompute civic opportunity score (0???1) or set to NA if no info
    civic_score = ifelse(
      (is.na(volunteer) & is.na(membership) & is.na(take_action) & is.na(events)) |
      (rowSums(across(c(volunteer, membership, take_action, events)), na.rm = TRUE) == 0),
      NA,
      idx_mean(volunteer, membership, take_action, events)
    ),
    # Bin organizations into civic opportunity score categories
    civic_score_group = case_when(
      is.na(civic_score)        ~ "No Civic Score", 
      civic_score < 0.5         ~ "Low Civic Score",
      civic_score >= 0.5        ~ "Median or High Civic Score"
    ),
    civic_score_group = factor(civic_score_group, levels = c(
      "No Civic Score", "Low Civic Score", "Median or High Civic Score"
    ))
  ) %>%
  # Group by civic score category and apply bootstrapped medians with CIs
  group_by(civic_score_group) %>%
  summarize(
    asset   = list(bootstrap_median_ci(asset_amt)),
    income  = list(bootstrap_median_ci(income_amt)),
    revenue = list(bootstrap_median_ci(revenue_amt)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 

# Reshape data to long format: one row per (score group × metric)
summary_df_long <- summary_df_long %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(asset, income, revenue),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "boot_result"
  ) %>%
  unnest_wider(boot_result, names_sep = "_")  # creates columns: median, ci_low, ci_high

# Confirm that all three civic score groups are present
unique(summary_df_long$civic_score_group)
```

### Figure 4

```{r}
################################################################################
# FIGURE 4
################################################################################

# Prettify metric names 
summary_df_long <- summary_df_long %>%
  mutate(metric = str_to_title(metric))  # e.g., "asset" → "Asset"

# Create the plot object
figure4_plot <- ggplot(summary_df_long, aes(x = factor(civic_score_group), y = boot_result_median, group = metric)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = metric), position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = boot_result_ci_low, ymax = boot_result_ci_high, color = metric),
    width = 0.3,
    linewidth = 1.5,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = metric),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = scales::label_dollar()(boot_result_median)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Civic opportunity score",
    y = "Median amount (excluding NAs and 0s)",
    fill = "Financial Metric",
    color = "Financial Metric",
    title = "Median Asset, Income, and Revenue by Civic Opportunity Score",
    subtitle = "95% confidence intervals are created by bootstrapping"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = NA)))

# Save as PNG
ggsave(
  filename = here("plots", "figure4.png"),
  plot = figure4_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 300
)

# Save as high-quality JPG
ggsave(
  filename = here("plots", "figure4.jpg"),
  plot = figure4_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 300
)
```

## The third dataset (who we are)

### County 

```{r}
# Normalize county-level covariates
# This is min-max normalization: (x - min) / (max - min)
cnts_civic_org_type <- cnts_civic_org_type %>%
  mutate(POV150 = normalize(POV150),
         SNGPNT = normalize(SNGPNT),
         BROAD = normalize(BROAD),
         NOHSDP = normalize(NOHSDP),
         UNEMP = normalize(UNEMP),
         REMNRTY = normalize(REMNRTY))

# Recode predicted class into two categories
cnts_civic_org_type <- cnts_civic_org_type %>%
  mutate(new_class = ifelse(str_detect(class, "Rel|Social"), "Religious or Social & Fraternal", "Others"))

# Compute share of religious/social orgs per county
cnts_civic_org_new_type <- cnts_civic_org_type %>%
  group_by(new_class, FIPS) %>%
  mutate(re_or_so_freq = sum(freq)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(FIPS, re_or_so_freq, POV150:REMNRTY) %>%
  distinct()

# Estimate OLS model for predictors of religious/social org share
sum_cnts_civic_org_type <- summary_class_civic_org(cnts_civic_org_new_type)
  
# Plot OLS estimates with 95% CIs (county-level)
cnty_type_plot <- sum_cnts_civic_org_type %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(name, estimate), y = estimate, ymax = conf.high, ymin = conf.low)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Unit: County",
    x = "",
    y = "Estimated OLS Coefficients",
    fill = "Civic opportunity organization type") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, col = "red", linetype = 2) 
```

### ZIP code 

```{r}
# Normalize ZIP code-level covariates
# This is min-max normalization: (x - min) / (max - min)
zcta_civic_org_type <- zcta_civic_org_type %>%
  mutate(POV150 = normalize(POV150),
         SNGPNT = normalize(SNGPNT),
         BROAD = normalize(BROAD),
         NOHSDP = normalize(NOHSDP),
         UNEMP = normalize(UNEMP),
         REMNRTY = normalize(REMNRTY))

# Recode predicted class into two categories
zcta_civic_org_type <- zcta_civic_org_type %>%
  mutate(new_class = ifelse(str_detect(class, "Rel|Social"), "Religious or Social & Fraternal", "Others"))

# Compute share of religious/social orgs per ZIP code
zcta_civic_org_new_type <- zcta_civic_org_type %>%
  group_by(new_class, ZCTA) %>%
  mutate(re_or_so_freq = sum(freq)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ZCTA, re_or_so_freq, POV150:REMNRTY) %>%
  distinct()

# Estimate OLS model for predictors of religious/social org share
sum_zcta_civic_org_type <- summary_class_civic_org(zcta_civic_org_new_type)

# Plot OLS estimates with 95% CIs (ZIP code-level)
zcta_type_plot <- sum_zcta_civic_org_type %>%
 ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(name, estimate), y = estimate, ymax = conf.high, ymin = conf.low)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Unit: ZIP code",
    x = "",
    y = "Estimated OLS Coefficients",
    fill = "Civic opportunity organization type") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, col = "red", linetype = 2)
```

```{r}
# Combine ZIP and county estimates into a single data frame
binded_sums <- bind_rows(sum_cnts_civic_org_type %>% 
            mutate(unit = "County"), 
                         sum_zcta_civic_org_type %>%
            mutate(unit = "ZIP code"))
```
